executiveSummary: GM0542's 2025 identity, centre, population, six neighbourhoods, one BAG place and BRT core, and two N210 municipal-border links are internally coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Krimpen lies between the tidal Nieuwe Maas and Hollandsche IJssel behind distinct primary and regional defences; the Hollandsche IJsselkering is a real control structure and the 10.5 km KIJK dike programme is under construction. The generic river preset applies 1.969298 m through T+72 and the coastal preset applies 1.102765 m at T+24 without selecting either water body, kering state, defence/breach, outside-dike footprint or recession. Generic pluvial forcing applies 0.754031 m without the low, subsided Oud-Krimpen drainage system or a governed stress-test surface. All eight individual hazards reuse the exact same six-neighbourhood ranking. On the audit reference date the Algerabrug is closed to ordinary motor traffic until 7 September 2026, with a separate emergency-services lane and temporary active-mode/Waterbus arrangements; the simulator retains the correct audited N210 crossing but lacks this time- and role-specific restriction. Public registers identify 113 water assets, Stedin/Oasen/Ziggo territories, one NBNL planning area, 37 antenna records, 16 education records and no local acute-care point, but do not establish live topology, state, backup or restoration. The VRR's own governance record describes 72-hour municipal self-sufficiency as a goal that was not yet current reality for smaller municipalities. Unsupported local precision must therefore be suppressed, and all missing, stale, out-of-coverage or role-ambiguous data remain Unknown/NoData rather than zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0542 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0542 as Krimpen aan den IJssel and reports 29,793 residents, density 3,882/km², 24.6% aged 65 or older and 4,155 one-person households; the generated centre [4.596344442793289, 51.915837752253246] is inside the 2025 boundary.

Six neighbourhood rows in one district sum to 29,800 residents, seven above the municipality total (+0.023%); households sum to 12,665 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 7,345. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 29,793 without rewriting the source rows.

BAG supplies one Krimpen aan den IJssel place and BRT one woonkern. BAG/PDOK place data are Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0. Administrative labels and centroids are not flood cells, drainage catchments, kering influence areas or service territories.

District-heating share and charging-station indicators cover 0/6 neighbourhoods. Publisher null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData, not zero. Annual residents do not measure commuters, bridge/ferry users, patients, workers or incident-time occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Hollandsche IJsselkering and tidal Hollandsche IJssel system
evidenceSources.edition: Current Rijkswaterstaat public asset and waterway pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The Hollandsche IJsselkering at Krimpen was the first completed Delta Work (1958) and protects the low-lying region. It has two approximately 80 by 12 metre steel gates, normally operates one gate and can use both in extreme conditions; Rijkswaterstaat manages it.

The Hollandsche IJssel is tidal up to the Waaiersluis and meets the Nieuwe Maas at Krimpen. A local water scenario must therefore distinguish these boundaries, kering operation, defence state, outside-dike exposure and any selected breach or overtopping mechanism.

Rijkswaterstaat public pages expose inconsistent summary closure thresholds/frequencies (2.25 m NAP and 3–4 times/year on the asset page versus 2.05 m and 2–3 times/year on another high-water page). No threshold should drive the simulator without a pinned operational source, datum, issue time and validity contract.

Static asset purpose and typical operation are planning/context evidence, not a live gate position, water-level forecast, defence guarantee or local inundation depth. No standard blanket reuse licence was identified on the pages.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard / Hoogwaterbeschermingsprogramma / Gemeente Krimpen aan den IJssel
evidenceSources.title: E03 — KIJK Hollandsche IJssel dike reinforcement and urban water/adaptation programmes
evidenceSources.edition: KIJK project page updated March 2026; GRP 2023–2027 and sustainability agenda 2025–2028
supports: KIJK strengthens 10.5 km of Hollandsche IJssel primary dike between Krimpen, Ouderkerk and Gouderak for height and stability during 2025–2031. The narrow dike carries the area's only through road, borders about 800 homes/businesses and contains cables/pipes. Programme need and works are not evidence of an acute failure.

Municipal information says cable and pipe relocation/replacement started from 13 April 2026 in phases. Construction, traffic and utility interfaces require dated segment status; a programme polygon or future completion cannot become a present closure, failure or capacity value.

The municipal GRP 2023–2027 assigns wastewater, rainwater and groundwater duties. Current adaptation documents identify improved drainage in Langeland and Oud-Krimpen, sewer replacement with street raising, green/retention measures and testing against heavier rainfall.

Oud-Krimpen contains old non-piled homes and subsided public space where streets cannot simply be restored to original elevation; the municipality describes water nuisance and a roughly 1,000-home waterproofing programme. This is strong local pluvial context but not a licensed machine-readable present-depth or drainage-state layer.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Gemeente Krimpen aan den IJssel
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current Algerabrug maintenance closure, role-specific passage and alternatives
evidenceSources.edition: Official closure period 10 August 2026 00:00 through 7 September 2026 05:00; inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The N210 Algerabrug is closed to ordinary motor traffic for urgent maintenance from 10 August 2026 00:00 through 7 September 2026 05:00. Rijkswaterstaat reports normal daily use of about 47,000 motor vehicles and 7,600 cyclists/pedestrians and an average 60-minute addition on the signed N210/N207/A20/N219 motor detour.

Emergency services retain passage on the reversible lane, while pedestrians and cyclists use a temporary bridge. These are separate role/mode states; neither an unrestricted link nor one blanket closed edge is correct.

Waterbus service between Stormpolder and Rivium was increased, including overnight provision, as mitigation. Static schedules and a planned increase do not prove incident-time vessel, berth, crew, passenger or evacuation capacity.

The high shipping opening is separately unavailable for roughly twelve weeks from 27 July; vessels low enough for the fixed bridge can pass. Transport status needs mode, class, direction, authority, issue/valid time and Unknown-after-expiry semantics. No blanket content reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regional crisis governance and 72-hour municipal continuity capability
evidenceSources.edition: Public governing-board minutes 10 December 2025; Crisisplan 2026–2029 adopted at that meeting
supports: The board adopted Crisisplan 2026–2029. The minutes record that a municipal crisis organisation able to sustain itself for 72 hours is a guideline/goal, but not then current reality for smaller municipalities; capacity and financial follow-up were still required.

This is authoritative governance and capability-planning evidence, not proof that Krimpen has or lacks a specific incident resource, nor a guarantee of staffing, relief, fuel, communications or autonomous continuity at any checkpoint.

The earlier regional risk profile separately recognises extreme rain, outside-dike flooding, inside-dike flooding and nature fire in a region structured by the Nieuwe Maas, Lek and Hollandsche IJssel. Its 2022–2025 period has ended, so it remains historical planning context rather than a current operational risk state.
The public record supports an explicit first-72-hour authority/action/resource/status ledger and Unknown defaults. No standard blanket machine-reuse licence was identified for the documents.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road and transit context plus cross-boundary acute care
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates two GM0542 border links: the previously audited N210/Algerabrug connection to Capelle aan den IJssel and N210 toward Krimpenerwaard. Nominal capacity 150 is a generalized scenario ceiling, not observed throughput or an emergency-services guarantee.

GTFS provides 43 stop areas, including Waterbus Stormpolder and Algerabrug. Static stop/schedule data do not establish running vehicles/vessels, accessible capacity, passenger loading, evacuation suitability, fuel, crew or restoration.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 contains no acute-care point inside GM0542. IJsselland Ziekenhuis in Capelle states that its emergency department operates 24/7; RIVM reports 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics, 12 treatment rooms and 22,924 visits in 2025.

The external facility depends materially on cross-boundary access, but registration and annual volume do not establish current acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup, ambulance passage, diversion or bed/treatment capacity. RIVM v1.1 is CC0; the hospital page does not state a blanket reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water, provider, grid-planning, antenna, education and current-observation context
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; contributor/provider dates vary
supports: Full CBS-boundary containment assigns 113 HWH records: 105 sewer pumps, five surface-water pumps and three weirs. Only eight name HHSK as manager, 105 report manager Unknown, 101 capacities are non-null and 12 null. Units, comparability, connected catchments, flow, control, power/backup and live state are not established. IMWA/DAMO is CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent coverage.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point lookup identifies Stedin electricity (updated 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025), Oasen drinking water (29 December 2025) and Ziggo media (7 September 2025); drainage is empty. A reference-point provider record is not municipal completeness, physical topology, live outage, quality, capacity or restoration.

One NBNL planning sample, CM48 Langeland, reports withdrawal 117 MW existing, 165 MW required and 0.7 MW/6 requests queued, no injection figures, TenneT categories 3/0 and 18 projects with earliest year 2026. This is planning context with no exact dataset licence identified, not live load, reserve, outage or project completion.

RDI supplies 37 antenna records (15 mobile, seven fixed links, 13 amateur and two broadcast), and daily CC-BY DUO RIO supplies 16 education records. Neither register proves coverage, backhaul, power, shelter role, occupancy, staff or supplies; the RDI service exposes no fixed standard licence/cadence in the consumed metadata.

The bounded deployment assigns no Waterinfo observation/forecast, NDW incident, KNMI weather observation/warning or seismic origin, or RIVM PM2.5 point inside GM0542. Each empty result is source/time/spatial NoData, not normal water/weather/air, open roads, zero seismic hazard or an all-clear.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent water and compound consequences lack hydraulics, role-specific access, operators and confirmed first-72-hour actions.
notes: River retains floodDepthM 1.969298 and severity 0.621416 through T+72; affected rises from 15,314 to 16,317 and burden reaches 1,098,798.34 while facilities falls from 0.495762 to 0.325198 without a selected event.

Compound retains floodDepthM 0.778580 at T+72; affected rises from 17,539 to 18,749, pressure from 0.557832 to 0.586663 and burden reaches 1,239,925.95 while facilities falls from 0.491408 to 0.285471.
Coastal direct forcing clears by T+72 but residual exact service values and 853,906.52 deprived person-hours lack recession/dewatering, access and operator-action evidence.

Every plateau, deterioration and recovery needs an event/action/resource ledger with authority, issue/observation/valid time, role/mode access and uncertainty; 72 hours is a preparedness horizon, not proof of self-sufficiency or recovery.

findings.summary: River and coastal presets produce false local hydraulic precision without selecting the relevant tidal system or defences.
findings.evidence: River holds 1.969298 m through T+72 with up to 16,317 affected people-equivalent; coastal gives 1.102765 m at T+24. Krimpen requires explicit Nieuwe Maas/Hollandsche IJssel boundary conditions, Hollandsche IJsselkering state, primary/regional defence or breach/overtopping, outside-dike footprint and recession. Static kering and KIJK evidence validates mechanisms, not amplitudes.
findings.action: Do not blanket-disable river or coastal risk, because both contributing families are locally plausible. Suppress decision-facing depths, affected counts and percentages until an authority-approved versioned event resolves water body, datum, boundary hydrograph, kering/defence state, footprint, uncertainty and valid time.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Stedin/Oasen/gas/telecom/wastewater topology, current control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Krimpen water outcomes depend on Nieuwe Maas/Hollandsche IJssel boundary conditions, kering and primary/regional defence state, possible breach/overtopping, outside-dike geometry, rain, subsidence/terrain, sewers, groundwater, internal water levels and pumps; static project/context pages are not forecasts.
HWH records have contributor-dependent coverage and incomplete managers/capacities; even non-null values lack enough unit/topology/control metadata for aggregation or causal use.
The active Algerabrug arrangements are time-, role- and mode-specific. Public plans do not guarantee emergency throughput, Waterbus capacity, detour performance or state beyond their stated validity.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM records omit commuters, bridge/ferry users, industrial workers, visitors, home-care needs, live hospital demand, shelters and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, kering, defence, drainage, weather, roads, care and utility states can change after audit completion; stale, empty or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
